fixes.explanation: Hands, friend. "Under their wings on their four sides they had human hands." (Ezekiel 1:8) That fits with the human form Ezekiel noticed when he first described them. All four living creatures had faces and wings too. Tucked under the wings on all four sides, that's a lot of hands.

True, friend. "As they moved, they went in any of the four directions, without pivoting as they moved." (Ezekiel 1:17) No turning around first, they just go. The creatures don't turn as they move either. Each one goes straight ahead. (Ezekiel 1:9)

A mountain feels big enough for this scene, friend. But Ezekiel sees something else above the expanse: the likeness of a throne with the appearance of sapphire. (Ezekiel 1:26) The text names a throne, and it never mentions a mountain.

Yes, friend. "…on the throne high above was a figure like that of a man." (Ezekiel 1:26) Ezekiel says the figure is "like" that of a man. That throne is the one above the expanse, with the appearance of sapphire.
A dove doesn't show up on this throne, friend. The text says that on the throne high above was "…a figure like that of a man." (Ezekiel 1:26) The throne itself has the appearance of sapphire.

A rainbow, friend. "The appearance of the brilliant light all around Him was like that of a rainbow in a cloud on a rainy day." (Ezekiel 1:28) Ezekiel says this was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD. Rainbows are my favorite color, so you know I'm glad it made the list.
Hail is a fair guess for a stormy cloud, friend. But the text says nothing about hail. It says the cloud has fire flashing back and forth, with brilliant light all around it.

Snow isn't in this vision, friend. Ezekiel sees "…a great cloud with fire flashing back and forth…" (Ezekiel 1:4) That's fire, not flurries. It's a whirlwind coming from the north, with brilliant light all around it.

That's the set, friend. Each one has a man's face, and also "…the face of a lion on the right side, the face of an ox on the left side, and also the face of an eagle." (Ezekiel 1:10) Four faces on one creature, just as verse 6 says. (Ezekiel 1:6)
Bear, goat and dove aren't in this vision, friend. The text names a lion on the right side, an ox on the left side, and an eagle. (Ezekiel 1:10) The man's face comes first. That's the full list.

A throne, friend. "Above the expanse over their heads was the likeness of a throne with the appearance of sapphire…" (Ezekiel 1:26) Notice the words "likeness" and "appearance" in that verse. The throne sits above the expanse over the creatures' heads.

A sunbeam is a nice picture, friend. But the text says the brilliant light around Him was "…like that of a rainbow in a cloud on a rainy day." (Ezekiel 1:28) Rain and sunbeams can go together, but the comparison Ezekiel gives is a rainbow.
That's what he does, friend. "…when I saw it, I fell facedown and heard a voice speaking." (Ezekiel 1:28) I think it was a lot to take in. And in that same verse, he hears a voice speaking.
